title: Fiberwise product counting bound
statement:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite types, let $P$ be a predicate on $\alpha$ and $Q$ a predicate on $\alpha \times \beta$, and let $C, B$ be natural numbers. Suppose that for every $a \in \alpha$ satisfying $P(a)$, the fiber $\{\,b \in \beta : Q(a,b)\,\}$ satisfies $\abs{\{\,b : Q(a,b)\,\}} \cdot C \le B$. Then
\[
\abs{\{\,(a,b) \in \alpha \times \beta : P(a) \wedge Q(a,b)\,\}} \cdot C
\;\le\;
\abs{\{\,a \in \alpha : P(a)\,\}} \cdot B .
\]
hypotheses_covered: α and β are finite types
P is a predicate on α
Q is a predicate on pairs in α × β
C and B are natural numbers
for every a with P(a), the fiber count of b satisfying Q(a,b) times C is at most B
replaced:
Let $P$ be a predicate on $\alpha$, $Q$ a predicate on $\alpha \times \beta$, and $C, B$ natural
numbers such that for every $a$ with $P(a)$ the fiber count satisfies
$\abs{\{b : Q(a,b)\}} \cdot C \le B$.  Then
\[
\abs{\{z \in \alpha\times\beta : P(z_1) \wedge Q(z_1,z_2)\}} \cdot C \;\le\;
\abs{\{a : P(a)\}} \cdot B .
\]
